Shoe Station Group Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results Business Wire Tue, November 24, 2026 at 3:10 AM PST 24 min read SHOE -21.78% FORT MILL, S.C., November 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Shoe Station Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: SHOE) (the "Company"), a leading omnichannel retailer of footwear and accessories for the family, today reported results for the third quarter ended October 31, 2026 and updated its Fiscal 2026 guidance. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights Net sales of $280.0 million compared to $297.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Shoe Carnival banner net sales declined 4.7 percent; Shoe Station banner net sales declined 7.7 percent. Sales in both banners were impacted by an increasingly promotional footwear marketplace and softer consumer demand following back-to-school. Gross profit margin of 31.9 percent, compared to 37.6 percent in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting increased promotional activity, liquidation of aged and excess inventory, and the prior-year benefit from raising prices in advance of tariff-related cost increases. Results include an approximately $18.0 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge; the charge will not result in any cash expenditures or affect the Company's cash flow or liquidity. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $116.0 million at quarter-end; the Company ended the third quarter of 2026 debt-free. Repurchased approximately $10.0 million of common stock during the third quarter; year-to-date 2026 capital returned to shareholders totaled approximately $31.1 million, inclusive of dividends. Full year 2026 net sales guidance and non-GAAP adjusted diluted earnings per share ("Adjusted EPS") guidance lowered to reflect results through the third quarter and current family footwear industry trends. "Our third quarter results were below the expectations we set in September. The improvement we saw in August did not carry into September and October. Families concentrated their spending around back-to-school, and then, as our advertising intensity lessened and fuel prices increased, consumer demand softened until cold weather arrived. Early results from our merchandising work are encouraging. Customers responded to our boot assortment as soon as the season opened, and those sales carried higher average unit retails and improved margins. Fall assortments that were curated to address localized demand began to arrive in our stores throughout the month of October," said Cliff Sifford, Interim President and Chief Executive Officer. "We enter the holiday season with the strongest boot assortment we have offered in years, intensified advertising, moderating fuel prices, and comparisons that ease as the quarter progresses. Our balance sheet remains strong. We are debt-free, we ended the quarter with $116 million in cash and marketable securities, and we returned capital to shareholders through our 58th consecutive quarterly dividend and the repurchase of approximately $10 million of our stock. We are managing this company for the long term, and the work underway in our assortments, our marketing, and our costs is aimed at returning this business to profitable growth," concluded Mr. Sifford. Credit: Below the Sky/Shutterstock.com. Sanofi has struck its biggest deal in over two decades after agreeing to buy US biopharma Insmed for $41bn in cash. The French drugmaker will pay $175 per share, representing a premium of around 17.5% on Insmed’s last price at market close on 23 November. Sanofi is funding the transaction through a combination of debt and cash on hand and has secured financing to support the deal. It is Sanofi’s largest deal since its $65bn merger with Aventis in 2004. Find out more The acquisition marks the most significant strategic move under CEO Belén Garijo, who took over at Sanofi in April this year. Garijo was tasked with turning around the company’s growth prospects after investors became increasingly concerned with vaccine headwinds and a lacklustre pipeline. Under prior CEO Paul Hudson, shares in the French drugmaker were trading around 30% down compared to highs in March 2025, though they already started to recover under Garijo’s leadership. Following the Insmed announcement, Sanofi’s shares surged 5.6% at market open on 24 November compared to the previous market close. The big pharma company has a market cap of €108.4bn ($118.5bn). In a research note, Citi analysts said: “We view the deal as strategically sensible.” Though they questioned whether it brings enough of an R&D platform to bolster Sanofi’s weak internal R&D going forward, alongisde the deal’s potential to limit further M&A capacity. In a statement, Garijo said: “I am delighted to welcome Insmed to Sanofi. This acquisition is a major strategic step to significantly accelerate our mid- and long-term growth trajectory and further strengthen our mid- and early-stage pipeline.” Sanofi will add two commercial therapies to its portfolio via the takeover. Brinsupri (brensocatib) is a once-daily, oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1) approved in multiple regions for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), a type of chronic lung condition. Brinsupri reached blockbuster status this year, generating over $1bn through the end of September. Sanofi said, “substantial additional growth is expected”. GlobalData, parent company of Pharmaceutical Technology, forecasts global sales of over $6bn in 2032. Sanofi also gains access to Arikayce (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), an inhaled antibacterial treatment used in combination with multidrug therapy for certain adults with mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease. It is the only approved inhaled therapy specifically indicated for treatment-refractory patients in the US, EU and Japan. Arikayce made $433.8m in 2025, growing 19% compared to 2024. While sales are growing, GlobalData forecasts it will only reach blockbuster status by 2032. The deal’s high price also reflects the extensive pipeline that will form a central pillar of Sanofi’s next phase of growth. Sanofi highlighted the Phase III programme evaluating treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP) across pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung diseases (ILDs). (NASDAQ:INSM) shares rose 14.3% in premarket trading on Tuesday after French pharmaceutical group Sanofi announced a binding agreement to acquire the US biopharmaceutical company for approximately US$41 billion in an all-cash transaction. Under the terms of the agreement, Sanofi will pay US$175 per Insmed share, representing a premium of approximately 46% to the company’s unaffected closing share price on 18 November 2026, before media reports of a potential acquisition emerged. What Is Sanofi Acquiring Through the Insmed Deal? The acquisition includes Insmed’s commercial medicines Brinsupri (brensocatib) and Arikayce (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), alongside its Phase 3 clinical development programme for treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP). TPIP is being developed for potential applications across multiple rare respiratory diseases. Insmed reported that Brinsupri, its treatment for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, generated US$1.09 billion in revenue through 30 September 2026, following its US commercial launch in August 2025. The acquisition expands Sanofi’s commercial respiratory medicines portfolio and clinical development pipeline. Why Is Sanofi Acquiring Insmed? The transaction forms part of Sanofi’s strategy to diversify its revenue sources ahead of the anticipated expiration of patent protection for Dupixent in 2031. Dupixent, a biologic treatment for inflammatory conditions including eczema and asthma, generated third-quarter revenue of €5.7 billion, accounting for nearly 40% of Sanofi’s total group sales. Sanofi Chief Executive Officer Belen Garijo described the acquisition as “a major strategic step to significantly accelerate our mid- and long-term growth trajectory and further strengthen our mid- and early-stage pipeline,” Insmed Chief Executive Officer Will Lewis said the transaction would “advance our commercial portfolio and phase 3 pipeline with a combined multibillion-dollar peak sales potential.” Sanofi expects the acquisition to contribute positively to its earnings per share starting in 2028. How Have Insmed Shares Responded to Acquisition Speculation? Insmed shares had already recorded substantial gains following media reports of Sanofi’s interest in acquiring the company. The stock rose approximately 20.6% on 19 November and gained a further 5.5% during Monday’s trading session. Tuesday’s confirmation of the binding acquisition agreement provided further clarity regarding the proposed transaction, bringing Insmed’s share price closer to the US$175 cash offer. Why Is Insmed Outperforming the Broader Market? Insmed’s premarket gains came against a weaker backdrop for US equities, with the S&P 500 declining 0.4%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.1% and the Nasdaq dropping 1%. The recent share price move tells you sentiment is in flux. Medtronic closed at US$100.72 after a 1-month share price return of 5.57% and a 90-day share price gain of 10.51%. However, the 1-year total shareholder return sits at just 0.83%, so momentum has picked up lately after a much flatter longer-run experience. That shift is happening around concrete catalysts. Clearance of the Hugo robotic-assisted surgery system for a broader set of general surgery procedures has refocused attention on Medtronic's longer-term procedure volume opportunity. In addition, the upcoming fiscal second quarter update is drawing attention to how quickly that platform might scale inside a US$122.3b medical devices group. On the other side of the ledger, investors are also absorbing a series of Class II recalls tied to Bluetooth disconnections in CareLink SmartSync device managers and related accessories. These issues relate to programming reliability rather than implant hardware, which helps explain why recent share price gains have continued. Even so, the events still feed into how the market prices execution risk around Medtronic's connected cardiac portfolio. After a sharp three month climb and fresh excitement around Hugo, Medtronic's share price already reflects a lot of hope. The next step is to work out how much upside is still on the table. According to LunaRodas, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the narrative, the key question is whether recent execution can carry the heavier expectations now being placed on the business. Medtronic's fiscal first quarter of 2027 arrived with 13.7% organic growth, a number that would be arresting in any quarter. This figure was inflated by an extra selling week that management estimates contributed roughly 670 basis points. Stripping out the calendar effect, the underlying figure still represents, by their own account, the strongest performance in nearly eight years.
